description-proc.eng: Tipperary County Council Clonmel Flood Defence Demountable Barrier Seal Replacement. The scope of this contract includes the replacement of demountable barrier seals and other associated works. Tipperary County Council, River Suir (Clonmel) Drainage Scheme, Replacement of Demountable Barrier Seals. In order to address long-term issues of flooding in Clonmel, the Office of Public Works (OPW) commissioned a study of the catchment area to develop sustainable options to address flood risk in the town and the surrounding areas. The overall flood defence scheme comprised of: • 3.8 km of flood walls • 3.5 km of embankments • 850 m of demountable defences • 5.9km of storm water sewers • 12 pumping stations • 2 fish passes • the replacement of three bridges • strengthening / widening of a further two Bridges. Work on the scheme was completed in 2013. As part of the construction of the flood defence scheme, there are a number of locations where demountable barriers are installed that are deployed during flood events. There are visible signs of these seals reaching the end of their operational life. The scope of this contract includes the replacement of demountable barrier seals and other associated works.

Le système de choppers sera utilisé à cette fin en combinaison avec un système de détection qui ne fait pas partie du présent appel d'offres. Le système de choppers ne sera installé de manière permanente dans aucun instrument, mais sera monté et démonté dans l'instrument souhaité selon le programme de mesures expérimentales. Das Chopper-System wird nicht fest in ein Instrument eingebaut, sondern entsprechend dem experimentellen Messprogramm in das gewünschte Instrument ein- und ausgebaut. Mehr Details in der Anforderungs-Spezifikation PSI-BP54-004 Rev. 1.1

description-proc.eng: This notice establishes a qualification system for economic operators capable of providing, by the long-term supply (by ownership or charter or an equivalent arrangement), the operation, management and maintenance of a Floating Storage and Regasification Unit (FSRU) and associated services to support Ireland’s Strategic Gas Emergency Reserve. The Qualification System comprises two lots: Lot 1 for long‑term strategic gas emergency reserve services using an FSRU (to be the subject of an Initial Competition), and Lot 2 for short‑term strategic gas emergency reserve services using an FSRU as a bridging vessel (which GNI may run only if required). Qualified operators must be able to supply an FSRU capable of delivering up to approximately 416 MMSCF/day of natural gas, with readiness to move from standby to full send out within 24 hours, and meeting the Irish gas transmission system gas quality specification and odorisation requirements, including delivery at pipeline entry pressures up to circa 85 barg and receipt of LNG via side by side ship to ship transfer. Outside emergency deployment, the FSRU will predominantly operate on standby with minimal routine regasification; periodic operation may be required for assurance and maintenance purposes. Associated onshore and marine infrastructure (including any jetty, onshore terminal and pipeline works) are not included within the scope of this qualification system and will be the subject of a separate procurement; however, the successful contractor(s) may be required to provide and/or coordinate necessary ancillary services to support safe and reliable operations, including catering services, crew logistics, waste and residue handling and offtake, fender storage and management, and utilities support as appropriate to FSRU operations. Contracts may be awarded to qualified operators without further publication. Further details, including technical, legal and financial requirements for qualification, are set out in the qualification system documents and will be further specified at call‑off stage.

title-proc.eng: Intention notice SCADA-system

description-proc.eng: Orkland municipality intends to enter into an ongoing contract with Autic System AS for the product Ignition - SCADA-system for water and sewage. Orkland municipality is holding the procurement without a competition as the procurement concerns services that only a specific supplier can deliver, because competition is impossible for technical reasons, cf. the Utilities Regulations § 9-3 b no. 2. Ignition is a full web-based SCADA platform, with HMI clients delivered as pure HTML5 applications that can be run in standard browsers on PCs, tablets and mobiles without local client installations or plugins. The system supports separate, logically separate projects/instances within the same platform, with each project being administered, developed and operated independently, but still under a joint gateway/server. The development environment included in the platform supports more than 10 simultaneous developers on the same system/project without additional licence costs per developer or user. The SCADA platform is widespread in the market, with a documented and broad ecosystem of certified integrators and developers in the Nordic region and internationally, so that the municipality is not dependent on one supplier, but can choose between several competent environments for further development and operation. The system has built-in support for SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect as authentication mechanisms, which enable integration with national ID systems such as BankID/Freja as well as the municipality ́s other IAM system. The SCADA system is module based, so functionality such as history (Historian), reporting, web HMI, alarm handling, SMS/email notification and edge/IIoT functions are delivered as separate modules within the same platform, and can be activated/disabled without replacing the system.

title-proc.eng: Intention notice water and sewage plan

description-proc.eng: Intention notice digital main plan for water and sewage in Orkland municipality. Orkland municipality intends to enter into an ongoing contract with W&S vision AS for a digital platform for the main water and sewage plan. Orkland municipality is holding the procurement without a competition as the procurement concerns services that only a specific supplier can deliver, because competition is impossible for technical reasons, cf. the Utilities Regulations § 9-3 b no. 2. VA-plan.no is a SaaS system that intends to connect data sources closer to strategic and tactical planning for the water and sewage system. It is a management system that will give both inhabitants, politicians and employees in the municipality better visibility into the own water and sewage system and the status of the investment work to be done. The water and sewage plan is a cloud based system and is designed for responsive web design for optimal viewing on various devices (PCs, terminal servers, tablets and mobiles). The water and sewage plan is the only ready system in the market that can deliver this system. The scope of the procurement is estimated to NOK 200,000,000 excluding VAT NOK 150,000 excluding VAT per annum - NOK 1.2 million over 8 years. This involves the uploading of substrates, such as the existing main plan, objectives, strategic initiatives and initiatives in the next 3 years. In addition to configuring data sources such as KOSTRA and the pipeline database, as well as training super users. Extra professional support is planned to be ordered to set up views for different user groups. Orkland municipality spends considerable costs updating the pipeline database and making good management plans. Good knowledge of the discipline is very important for creating good overviews of different user groups. Va visjon AS is the only actor who currently provides this service, a competition for other suppliers cf. The supply regulations §9-3 b no. 2. The contracting authority intends to enter into a contract with W&S vision AS 18.02.2026. It is intended to enter a contract for a framework agreement for a period of 8 years, with 6 months termination during the agreement period. Any objections are to be sent to Orkland kommune via the Mercell portal by 16 February.

description-proc.eng: Wexford County Council invites responses from economic operators who are interested in participating in this competitive dialogue procurement process for the delivery of a high quality mixed-use urban quarter on County Council owned lands at Trinity Wharf, Wexford. The Competition is being run in accordance with the European Union (Award of Public Authority Contracts) Regulations 2016 (S.I. No. 284 of 2016). The tender outlines the vision for Trinity Wharf and the factors that make it a such a unique opportunity. Located between Wexford Harbour and Wexford town centre, with panoramic waterfront views, the scheme aims to regenerate a derelict brownfield site, transforming it into a first-class mixed-use urban quarter, with sustainability at its core. The current Trinity Wharf master plan incorporates three commercial office blocks, a hotel and conference/cultural centre, residential units, marina, retail offering and a multi-storey car park. Together, these components will integrate with a network of attractive public realm infrastructure and amenities, designed around a focal public realm plaza. It is intended that Trinity Wharf will be a new centre for leisure, tourism and economic development in Wexford Town. However, Wexford County Council is open to considering a proposal which includes some (but not necessarily all) of these elements, or alternatively, a mix of these elements, depending on the viability of the proposal. The Trinity Wharf development is a key component of Wexford County Council’s economic development strategy. This is reflected in the planning policies of the Wexford County Development Plan 2022-2028, which are explicitly backed by the Plan’s Strategic Objectives. Due to the constraints of the template form, this contract has been described as a “works” contract, and the form of contract has been stated to be “PWCF2 Works Contract Designed by the Contractor”. However, in reality, this opportunity is not a traditional works contract. Rather, Wexford County Council is seeking proposals from developers as to the development of a high quality mixed-use urban quarter on County Council owned lands at Trinity Wharf, Wexford, with the expectation that elements that will form part of that development will evolve during the dialogue process depending on the viability of the proposal. For this reason, the competitive dialogue process has been chosen, with the intention to use a bespoke form of contract (which will be subject to the dialogue process). Applicants should disregard statements to the contrary in this contract notice, which are a feature of the constraints on completing the template form. Candidates should also note that the standard Contract Notice wording required that Wexford County Council choose from certain pre-populated options as to the form of contract. However, noting the nature of this opportunity, and the fact that this is a development and regeneration project (rather than a traditional works contract), the listed options are not appropriate. Candidates should therefore disregard the reference to PW-CF2. The form of contract to be entered into will likely be a bespoke form of development agreement which will be subject to dialogue during the dialogue phase. Candidates should note that the form of development agreement may be structured in phases or packages, which may envisage delivery of the opportunity pursuant to distinct call off contracts. While the final form of agreement is not yet determined, Candidates should note that it may take the form of a single development agreement or a form which is more akin to a single-supplier framework agreement. Further detail will be provided at dialogue stage.
